A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) nitrogen limitation reduces CO2 uptake by regrowing forests, 2) the impact is greater for future projections than for historical simulations, 3) the impact is sensitive to nitrogen inputs, and 4) this is a critical factor in estimating future LULUC emissions and the effectiveness of land-based carbon mitigation strategies.
the IPCC Fifth Assessment estimates for LULUC emissions for future scenarios are likely to be underestimated, and this underestimation is likely to increase in the 21st Century.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the IPCC scenarios underestimate LULUC emissions because they do not include nitrogen limitation of carbon uptake in forests.

the inclusion of nitrogen limitation in Earth System Models is essential to improve the accuracy of future LULUC emissions projections, which in turn is important for the design of mitigation policies.
